mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals weakening aggregate demand but a relative strength in housing, which historically precedes a muted S&P 500 response over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between the trigger and returns drops below 0.2.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.2% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that depress consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average while the S&P 500 earnings proxy (RSAFS) remains flat signals supply-side constraints that are not yet reflected in earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.20) when INDPRO falls below its 6-month MA and RSAFS is flat.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in the federal funds rate below 3% signals an emergency easing that immediately boosts risk asset valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 3% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) following a monthly FEDFUNDS drop below 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both Personal Income (implied by GDPC1 growth) and Housing Starts (HOUST) above their respective 3-month moving averages signals a broad-based demand recovery that precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both GDPC1 and HOUST exceed their 3-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of four consecutive months with PAYEMS > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months, irrespective of monetary policy stance, signals entrenched supply weakness that ultimately produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
